Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing for LumenScale (LUM-2026-017) - sizing notes

Thanks Tessa — reviewed the spreadsheet. High-level sizing assumptions and recommendation below (short version):

Customer workload: mixed chat + generation with batch embedding/rerank jobs overnight. Peak online concurrency target = 1,000 concurrent requests with average prompt+response ~1,200 tokens (including prefix).
Model profile: customer expects to run a 70B dense model (LLM-v2 family). We should size for 70B serving at quantized fp16/8 where possible.

Sizing estimate (safety buffer included):
- Steady throughput baseline: ~1k concurrency => continuous tokens/sec estimate ~120k tokens/s across fleet.
- Recommended capacity: 18x H100-80GB class GPUs (or equivalent 36x L40s depending on availability) exposed as a dedicated pool with 2-token-prefetch KV caching per instance and request-level batching configured to 4-8 where permissible.
- Burst headroom: add 20% (4 additional H100-equivalent slots) to support unexpected traffic and canary testing.
- Warm-up: pre-warmed KV caches for top-50 prefixes per customer; expected pre-warm memory footprint ~400GB across the pool.

Operational impact:
- Expected per-token latency at target concurrency with continuous batching: median 65-90ms, tail (p95) 180-250ms depending on prompt length and batching.
- If we convert to smaller GPUs (L40), concurrency will require proportionally more instances and increase inter-node KV traffic; prefer H100-class if we must guarantee latency SLOs.

I'll attach a compact CSV in the internal drive with per-instance estimates. If we approve a 30-day hold, plan for the 18 H100-equivalents + 4 headroom reservation.

— Marcus
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing for LumenScale (LUM-2026-017) - cost & impact

Quick cost note based on Marcus's sizing:

- Reservation estimate (30 days): capex-equivalent billing for 22 H100-equivalent slots = ~$420k list price (this is illustrative; final depends on supplier pricing and any existing reserve credits).
- Pre-warm networking and egress: expect a one-time pre-warm bandwidth charge ~ $3k and storage for KV pre-warm snapshots ~ $1.2k.
- Opportunity cost: holding 22 slots reduces capacity available for other late-stage deals; recommend marking this pool as "soft reserved" and enabling automatic auto-fallback rules if utilization for higher-priority deals hits 85% fleet-wide.

Suggested customer-visible approach: 1) 30-day soft hold with a nominal reservation fee (we propose 10% of estimated reservation value, billed upfront and refundable against committed capacity if they convert), 2) MoU outlining required lead times for conversion to committed capacity, 3) Canary window dates and acceptance criteria.

Attaching a brief cost summary: cost_estimate_breakdown.pdf

— Grace
Director, Customer Reliability & Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing for LumenScale (LUM-2026-017) - ops playbook

Operational checklist for a 30-day soft hold (concise):
1) Mark capacity: tag 22 H100-equivalent slots as LUM-2026-017_softhold in the resource catalog.
2) Reserve pre-warm storage: snapshot KV caches and allocate 500GB ephemeral storage across pool nodes.
3) Scheduling: block maintenance windows for the softhold pool; allow hotfixes but no rolling upgrades during hold unless critical.
4) Fallback policy: if fleet utilization >85% for 48h, trigger automated reallocation with 72h notice to AE and customer.
5) Monitoring: add customer-specific dashboards (latency, token-rate, cache hit-rate) and alert thresholds p95 latency >300ms or cache hit <70%.
6) Hand-off: assign a single ops owner (recommended: Logan) and an engineering on-call (Marcus) for the 30-day window.

If sales confirms the reservation fee and legal signs an MoU, we'll enact the tag and start pre-warm procedures within 48 hours.

— Logan
Head of Capacity Operations
Redwood Inference
